title: Correct answer with clear reasoning
label: Demo data — synthetic
question: Why is the limit of (x^2 - 1)/(x - 1) as x approaches 1 equal to 2, even though direct substitution gives 0/0?
student_answer: Direct substitution yields the indeterminate form 0/0. Since we are evaluating the behavior as x approaches 1 and x != 1, we factor the numerator into (x - 1)(x + 1), cancel the common (x - 1) factor, and evaluate lim (x + 1) = 2.

chunks.text: When direct substitution results in the indeterminate form 0/0, algebraic simplification such as factoring (x^2 - 1) = (x - 1)(x + 1) allows evaluating the limit for x approaching c without requiring f(c) to be defined.
